name: Silt Night
description: Observed on November 3rd, Silt Night commemorates the 2201 Lake Michigan Surge — a catastrophic storm event compounded by failed seawall infrastructure that flooded the lower Shelf wards and killed an estimated 14,000 residents over four days, most of them Tier 1. The name comes from the grey-brown silt that coated every surface when the water receded, and the way survivors described finding their neighbors preserved in it like fossils. Across M88, people leave grey-painted stones or grey cloth strips on windowsills, doorframes, and fence posts — a gesture that began spontaneously in the Shelf and spread upward through the tiers over two decades.
cultural_impact: Silt Night is one of the only traditions that genuinely crosses all tiers without corporate mediation, though the way each tier observes it reveals exactly how much distance wealth creates from catastrophe. The grey-stone practice has become so widespread that stone-painters in the Shelf now sell hand-painted Silt stones year-round, one of the Shelf's most consistent informal economies.
key_figures: Nneka Osei-Boateng (Shelf Ward 4 community organizer who coordinated the first Silt Night vigil in 2202)
Architect Pemba Volkov (designed the Silt Memorial Substructure, a controversial underground monument the corponations tried to demolish in 2208)
Journalist Tariq Alves-Nkosi (whose illegal broadcast of the flood's first 48 hours is still circulated in the Underworld)
locations: The Silt Line (a painted grey stripe along the old flood boundary in Shelf Ward 4-7)
Lake-Edge Observation Deck, Tier 3 (the 'polite' observation point used by upper tiers)
story_hooks: A newly appointed corponation infrastructure auditor discovers that sealed internal documents prove the seawall failure was known about and deliberately unfunded for cost reasons — and someone is willing to pay a great deal to keep that buried.

A Shelf artist collective is planning to project the names of all 14,000 dead onto the Spire's exterior on the 25th anniversary of the Surge, and they need someone to get past the building's defensive countermeasures.

A Tier 5 family whose Spire-level apartment was completely unaffected by the Surge has quietly been funding the Silt Memorial for fifteen years anonymously — and their reasons are not purely altruistic.
origin_event: The 2201 Lake Michigan Surge, a four-day flood event that killed 14,000 Tier 1 residents and exposed the corponations' deliberate neglect of lower-ward infrastructure.
tier_observations: Tier 1 Shelf communities hold all-night vigils with candles floated in grey water bowls, recite names of the dead aloud, and share food communally — the most intimate and raw expression of the day. Tier 2 and 3 observe quietly with window stones and a moment of silence at sunset, many of them having lost distant relatives. Tier 4 treats it as a solemn but brief acknowledgment — a grey ribbon pinned to a lapel. Tier 5 Spire residents largely ignore it or attend a sanitized 'civic reflection breakfast' hosted by one of the corponations, though a small number are known to descend to the Shelf wards incognito to witness the vigils firsthand.
